title: How To Reach The Heart Of Difficult Students And Change Behavior
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that consistent, friction-free follow-through on a classroom management plan solves nearly all ordinary behavior problems, but chronically difficult students require one additional ingredient. That ingredient is treating every day as a fresh start: enforcing consequences without lecturing, scolding, or emotional friction, then greeting the student warmly and without grudge the moment the next day begins. He is careful to distinguish this from letting students off the hook, which he says only reinforces their sense of being different and not good enough. Instead, teachers must hold the line on consequences while simultaneously offering genuine daily kindness — a smile, a fist bump, and clear signals that the teacher has not given up. He describes this combination of unwavering accountability plus relentless daily forgiveness as what actually reaches a difficult student's heart and activates intrinsic motivation to change.
points: Friction-free follow-through on a classroom plan solves most ordinary behavior problems by removing personal conflict from consequences.
Difficult students need an added ingredient: treating every day as a genuinely new day regardless of prior misbehavior.
Letting students off the hook is not compassion — it reinforces their belief that they can't behave like everyone else.
Daily kindness (a smile, a fist bump) combined with strict accountability is what activates a difficult student's intrinsic motivation.
Once a consequence is served, the incident must be fully let go, with no residual coldness carried into the next interaction.
quotes: Your classroom management plan is set in stone. There is no going back. There is no negotiation, no capitulation, no surrender.
It is follow-through without friction that causes students to reflect on their mistakes, take responsibility for them, and resolve not to make them again.
It’s to make sure that every day is a new day and that every moment is a new moment for them to change and turn over a new leaf.
Failing to hold them accountable only hurts them and reinforces the image they have of themselves as different.
You must be relentless in your daily forgiveness, acceptance, and accountability while letting them in on the same jokes and banter as you do everyone else.
That’s it. That’s what reaches the heart and begins churning the intrinsic motivational engines that power the desire to do better and be better.
